As PZ-7 has the same animation model as AP-5 in ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'', she must therefore also be an RA-7 [[protocol droid]]. |class=[[Protocol droid]] |cost= |length= |width= |height=1.7 [[meter]]s''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' establishes that [[Protocol droid|droids]] of the [[RA-7 protocol droid]] line stand 1.7 [[meter]]s in height. As PZ-7 is depicted as an RA-7 droid in "[[Double Agent Droid]]" (see reference 2), she must therefore also stand 1.7 meters tall. |mass= |gender=[[Gender|Feminine programming]]{{Rebels|Double Agent Droid}} |pronouns= |sensor=[[Color|White]] |plating=Dark gray |armament= |equipment= |affiliation=*[[Galactic Empire]] **[[Imperial Security Bureau]] }} {{Quote|Halt. What are you doing here? I am PZ-7. I was not aware two inventory units were assigned to this level.|PZ-7, to AP-5|audio=PZ-7-Halt.flac|}} '''PZ-7''' was a [[Gender|feminine]] [[RA-7 protocol droid]] who served the [[Galactic Empire]] in [[2 BBY]] as an [[inventory droid]] at [[Killun Station]], an [[Imperial Security Bureau]] base located on the [[moon]] [[Killun 71]]. When the Imperial-turned-[[Alliance to Restore the Republic|rebel]] inventory [[Protocol droid|droid]] [[AP-5]] was [[Mission to recover Imperial codes|sent]] to Killun Station to secure clearance codes crucial to the Rebellion's planned attack on the [[planet]] [[Lothal]], he encountered PZ-7 before he could access the facility's [[Central Computer Core]]. PZ-7 told AP-5 that she had not been informed that a second inventory droid was stationed on that level. In response, AP-5 devised a lie that PZ-7 had been reassigned to Killun Station's cargo platform and that he was replacing her. After telling AP-5 that she understood, PZ-7 departed for her new posting, allowing her replacement to retrieve the secret codes for the Rebellion. ==Biography== {{Quote|Uh, well, it is unfortunate, but I must report, you have been reassigned to the cargo platform. I am your replacement.''"
"''I understand.|AP-5, to PZ-7|audio=AP-5-PZ-7.flac|}} PZ-7 was a [[Gender|feminine-programmed]] [[RA-7 protocol droid]] manufactured by [[Arakyd Industries]]. She served the [[Galactic Empire]] at the [[Imperial Security Bureau]] base [[Killun Station]], located on the [[moon]]{{Databank|killun-71|Killun 71}} [[Killun 71]], in [[2 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of "[[Double Agent Droid]]" to [[2 BBY]]. PZ-7 worked as an [[inventory droid]] on the level of the facility that housed its [[Central Computer Core]]. [[File:PZ-7_cargo_platform.png|thumb|left|225px|AP-5 tells PZ-7 that she has been reassigned to Killun Station's cargo platform.]] [[Phoenix Cell|Phoenix Squadron]], one of the cells that made up the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] against the Empire, made plans to destroy the Imperial [[Imperial Armory Complex|factory]] on the''[[Star Wars Rebels: Steps Into Shadow]]'' [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]]{{Databank|lothal|Lothal}} [[Lothal]] with the aid of [[Massassi Group|another rebel cell]].{{Rebels|An Inside Man}}{{Rebels|Zero Hour}} Before the rebels could initiate their attack, however, they required clearance codes for Lothal that could be accessed from Killun Station. To retrieve the codes, they [[Mission to recover Imperial codes|dispatched]] former [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot|Imperial pilot]] [[Wedge Antilles]], former Imperial inventory [[Protocol droid|droid]] [[AP-5]], and [[C1-series astromech droid|astromech droid]] [[C1-10P]] to the Imperial Security Bureau base. Once the rebels entered Killun Station, AP-5 made his way to the Central [[Computer]] Core, where the clearance codes were held. Before he could enter the room in which the core was located, however, he was stopped by PZ-7, who noted that she had not received word of a second inventory [[droid]] assigned to that level. In order to maintain his cover, AP-5 devised a lie, telling PZ-7 that she had been reassigned to Killun Station's cargo platform and that he was replacing her. PZ-7 told AP-5 that she understood and departed for her new posting, allowing him to retrieve the codes for the Rebellion from the Central Computer Core. ==Characteristics== {{Quote|I can't ''believe'' I'm the same model as that Imperial drone.|AP-5, about PZ-7|audio=AP-5-ImperialDrone.flac|}} A loyal Imperial droid, PZ-7 was quick to stop AP-5 and question why he was on the level she had been stationed at in Killun Station. However, when AP-5 stated that she had been reassigned elsewhere, PZ-7 fell for his trick, expressing no doubt in the validity of his fib. Once she departed for the base's cargo platform, AP-5 remarked to himself that he could not believe he was the same model as PZ-7, whom he disparaged as an Imperial drone. Like all RA-7 protocol droids, PZ-7 stood 1.7 [[meter]]s tall. She had dark plating and [[sensor]]s that would light up [[Color|white]] when she spoke. Etched on her forehead was a triangular-like design, inside of which was a dark circle containing a horizontal oval marking, with twelve petal-like shapes protruding from all around the circle. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:PZ-7_concept_art.png|thumb|right|200px|Concept art of PZ-7]] PZ-7 appeared in the nineteenth episode of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''{{'}} [[Star Wars Rebels Season Three|third season]], "[[Double Agent Droid]],"{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/double-agent-droid-episode-guide|text="Double Agent Droid" Episode Guide | Star Wars Rebels}} which aired on [[March 11]], [[2017]], on [[Disney XD]].{{TVcom|url=shows/star-wars-rebels/double-agent-droid-3447914|text=Star Wars Rebels - Season 3, Episode 18: Double Agent Droid}} She was voiced by [[Vanessa Marshall]], who also voices [[Hera Syndulla]], one of the show's main characters. Concept art of PZ-7 by [[Amy Beth Christenson]] dated [[February 16]], [[2016]], in which PZ-7 is depicted with black plating, was released on [[StarWars.com]] as part of the Episode Guide for "Double Agent Droid." ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|soundcat=Audio files of PZ-7|imagecat=Images of PZ-7}} *{{Rebels|Double Agent Droid}} {{1st}} ==Sources== *{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/double-agent-droid-episode-guide|text="Double Agent Droid" Episode Guide | Star Wars Rebels}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |ja=PZ-7 |nl=PZ-7 |pl=PZ-7 }} [[Category:Droids with feminine programming]] [[Category:Imperial Security Bureau droids]] [[Category:RA-7 protocol droids]]
